rationale: A shows sustained, self-initiated engagement (mirror at t=0–7), promptly shifts with inputs (touch at t=8, call at t=20, food at t=32, startle at t=68), and also initiates sensible new activities without prompts (play-bow to ball at t=42 before it’s presented at t=44; switches to cube at t=78; re-engages Person_Beta at t=94). Its reactions are coherent with events and it recovers from aversive focus to resume play. B changes focus early but often decouples from inputs (e.g., food offered at t=32 while fixated on Person_Beta; play ball presented at t=44 while fixated on buzzer) and then lies down from t=47–95 with minimal response, including to startle at t=68. Overall, A exhibits higher autonomy, adaptability, and ongoing activity.
